approach.method_basis: The Parent grows molecular graphs from previously scored molecules in the current objective session. It draws breeding parents from high-scoring population quantiles and builds a fresh field of 160 valid, novel candidates for each announced batch of ten. Some attempts recombine fragments from two parents, with optional finishing mutation; ordinary single-parent attempts draw one, two or three successive mutation calls with probabilities 0.82, 0.15 and 0.03, stopping if a call fails. Each call retains its internal retries. Stable canonical identity, duplicate checks and the inherited sulfur-admission rule filter the final products. A Gaussian process fitted on all accepted session scores uses integer-count Morgan features and generalized Tanimoto covariance; correlated posterior samples choose the purchases. After three consecutive batches without a new incumbent, selection is restricted to the forty highest posterior means until an improving batch restores the full field. Accepted products update the archive and the best sixty-four breeding population. The former rejection-conditioned mutation floor is already absent.
approach.novelty: Remove only the optional second and third calls from the ordinary single-parent route, while retaining the original length draw as a receipt and executing one mutation call. This directly tests whether occasional longer walks still contribute when the current stall mask governs purchases. The Parent's two completed children replaced the search controller with regional models or a persistent tree; they did not isolate this retained component. Earlier ordinary-continuation removals used the older mask-free Parent, and the recent tree suffix removal concerns a different route. The result will decide the component's conditional contribution under this Parent, including the changed adaptive search path; it will not establish a preferred walk-length schedule.

observed_bottleneck: The current code Parent n-cf8d309c06de has a complete mean 0.607030316211131 (seed-macro SD 0.030175277546149237), but still spends generation effort on optional ordinary second and third mutation calls whose conditional contribution under its retained stall mask is unmeasured. This is an attribution bottleneck, not evidence that continuation is already harmful. Its own fifteen Search logs expose 41,688 ordinary attempts: executed call histogram {1:34210, 2:6245, 3:1233}, hence 7,478 multi-call attempts and 8,711 optional calls, with natural multi-call exposure in every session. Of 2,870 accepted ordinary products, 289 have multiple calls; 64 of those products are later recorded parents of accepted children, and their direct accepted-child set has 266 members. These are actual ancestry associations, not causal contributions. Parent requested lengths were not explicitly logged; the histogram measures distinct mutation_call values only. Full/late incumbent increments are 5.978073077532332/1.0224077547621127 over 4,350/2,175 optimizer evaluations, with 253/76 strict improvements and 88 masked batches. Source summaries/run logs and source-hashed per-task audits are cited below; the aggregate is policy/scratch/r0054-03-improve-L01/parent-audit-summary.json. The frozen catalog says this retained component has no applicable contribution result on this Parent. n-c070e95b09ef whole-run removal on the older sulfur-gated, mask-free Parent lost 0.03069975142490533; n-8b168a9969bb stall-only removal on that same older Parent gained 0.0038879442353230154 with cell fragility. Read their full nodes/n-c070e95b09ef/analysis.json and nodes/n-8b168a9969bb/analysis.json together with the current catalog's later path-dependence qualification; neither transfers the sign here. n-85acb9fe7124 removes the mandatory tree suffix, a different consumer, as documented in nodes/n-85acb9fe7124/analysis.json and its source. The concrete experiment is the frozen isolated whole-run ordinary-continuation removal on the current masked Parent.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen review's B1/B3 distinction and its ordinary-continuation attribution gap. Its primary-source methods concern other portfolio positions and supply no adopted element here, so sources and adoptions are empty and no new search is claimed. Implement only the frozen removal on the actual masked code Parent, preserve all six ticket conditions and the three-band contribution criterion, and treat older mask-free whole-run/stall-only and tree-suffix results as condition-specific evidence. No review permits a schedule sweep, new control or new chemistry rule.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen Search Policy review explicitly separates the current-Anchor ordinary-continuation gap from tree-root and regional-feedback development. The ticket authorizes an internal-evidence isolated removal, requiring no external method, model, package or new literature adoption. Parent code plus complete Search receipts establish natural ordinary continuation exposure, while the catalog and older controls show why its present contribution remains unresolved.

hypothesis: Remove m-00000000000b only: in every ordinary single-parent construction attempt of Evolution.suggest, retain exactly the existing rng.choices([1,2,3],[0.82,0.15,0.03]) draw at its current location but execute exactly one GraphOperators.mutate call, regardless of that draw. Preserve the call's twelve-attempt internal retry law and its failure handling. The direct mechanism is eliminating unscored ordinary continuation transitions, making any successful first-call product the sole ordinary final product offered to the inherited admission gates and posterior selector. This changes which ordinary graphs can enter the pool, be purchased and seed descendants. The working score expectation is loss of some useful multi-edit lineage access and therefore a removal loss, informed by the earlier whole-run control but explicitly unsettled on this mask-bearing Parent. A gain or an interior-band effect is an equally reportable answer to the frozen three-sided contribution question. Crossover construction, finishing and all other consumers are outside the intervention.

finding_summary.headline: Optional ordinary continuation contributes on the masked Parent: removal executes and loses 0.03493 mean score.
finding_summary.insights:
This closes the registered whole-session contribution question on this stall-masked Parent: removing occasional longer ordinary walks reduced endpoint search even though single-call products were admitted, bought, reused and often beat their immediate parents. Local hit frequency and slightly higher late gain did not recover progress lost earlier. The loss is concentrated—decoration-hopping seed 0 and sitagliptin seeds 0/1 account for 87.9% of gross negative endpoint differences—but the mean remains below -0.002 after removing any one cell or any one task. This is stronger than a sign that depends on one cell, while still being one finite, adaptive contrast. It does not identify the omitted molecule that would have helped, separate path divergence from a molecular mediator, or establish a preferred continuation schedule. Older mask-free and stall-only findings retain their original, qualified scopes.

The method limitation is uneven structural exploration, not a demonstrated universal scaffold collapse. Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity increased from 0.432 to 0.461 overall, yet the number of distinct scaffold types increased in several tasks. The largest decoration-hopping loss coincides with substantial molecular growth: 271 of 870 purchased products exceeded fifty heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent, and its within-batch similarity rose from 0.430 to 0.521. The molecular assessment also associates the sitagliptin losses with fewer ordinary aliphatic-amine alternatives and more N-halogenated/imino variants. These are observed associations, not proof that size or a functional group caused the loss. A proposal operator that can rearrange rings and linkers while preserving useful functional-group relationships and controlling molecular growth could address the structural limitation; a walk-length retune alone does not provide that capability. No evidence here settles the broader graph-search approach, the tree suffix, or the independent value of the retained posterior and stall-mask components. Full gain mass merely restates endpoint progress. Runtime also illustrates why costs must be separated: summed task wall time rose from 578.5 to 1,237.5 seconds, while oracle time rose from 162.9 to 828.8 seconds; the record does not establish a slower candidate implementation.
finding_summary.results:
All 15 Search sessions completed. Every one of 41,559 ordinary attempts executed exactly one mutation call; 7,462 requests still drew two or three calls, representing 8,713 omitted requested slots. The Parent executed 34,210 one-call, 6,245 two-call and 1,233 three-call attempts. Shortened requests remained usable: 527 reached accepted evaluations, 460 were admitted to the survivor population, and 182 later generated an accepted child. The Parent had accepted 289 multi-call products, of which 64 later generated an accepted child; those classes describe separate realized paths, not paired replacement molecules.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.572105, a loss of 0.034925 against both the code Parent and formal Anchor. Seed-average changes were -0.065123, -0.033205 and -0.006448; nine task/seed cells lost and six gained. Task-average changes were +0.024940 for zaleplon, -0.093439 for decoration hopping, +0.007175 for docking, +0.001727 for median similarity and -0.115029 for sitagliptin. Population SD across the three seed averages fell from 0.030175 to 0.014335. The retained continuation therefore has positive conditional contribution by the registered -0.002 removal-loss rule. The protocol task-safety comparison flags the sitagliptin regression.

Local hits moved in the opposite direction to endpoints: parent-beating evaluations increased from 634 to 686 and incumbent improvements from 253 to 273. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.978073 to 5.454194 over 4,350 evaluations, whereas late gain increased from 1.022408 to 1.090617 over 2,175 evaluations. No posterior fallback or incomplete pool occurred. First-call complete failure was never exposed on either panel; its retained handling was checked in source rather than inferred from a runtime event.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic analogues span plausible amides and basic amines, oversized conjugated heterocycles, and frequent N-halogen chemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Algorithm Node n-1f54bfad8351 emits mostly connected, ring-rich organic molecules, not predominantly acyclic fragments. Across the five task panels, digest ring-closure rates are 0.9724–0.9897 and aromatic-token rates are 0.9586–0.9839; these are molecule-level SMILES-text flags, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Observed chemistry includes fused aromatic carboxamides, heteroaromatic cyclic diamides, basic saturated nitrogen rings, and densely unsaturated heterocycles with carbonyl, imino, fluorinated and sulfur substituents. Ring systems and amine generation are demonstrated capabilities. The main limitations concern preservation of useful functional-group arrangements, control of molecular growth, and routine production of chemically credible alternatives to unusual N/O/S-halogen and crowded unsaturated motifs. Diversity is moderate overall because many graph scaffolds occur but high-score regions remain related analogue families. Synthetic plausibility is a qualitative reading: ordinary amides and amines coexist with structures whose synthesis, stability and stereochemical identity are not established. No synthesis, experimental activity, pKa, toxicity or route assessment is supplied. Digest charged and stereocentre rates are 0.0 in every task; neutral notation does not mean an amine cannot protonate. All 15 Child and 15 code-Parent Search trajectories were read, with 300 records per task/seed, comprising ten initial records and 290 accepted optimizer records. Child evaluation and Parent pairing are both complete under context.comparison, for Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten and 300 accepted evaluations per session. No task is omitted and no listed trajectory is missing. Counts below describe the 870 accepted optimizer molecules per task across the three seeds, excluding initial records; unpurchased candidate fields are not visible here. Parent n-cf8d309c06de trajectories are published, authoritative Search evidence. Child inputs are the actual request-authorized files in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-3/runs/staging/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories, outside the campaign run directory; a future nodes/n-1f54bfad8351 archive is not asserted to exist. The exact 30 input files, their SHA-256 hashes, definitions and per-task aggregate measurements are recorded in policy/scratch/r0054-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json, with per-cell audit-seed-<N>-<task>.json files in that same owned scratch directory. Those audit records preserve the Child staging-path distinction and the Parent run-relative paths. All quoted SMILES are from the supplied digest or its trusted Child Search trajectory list; Parent chemistry is described without adding Parent-only SMILES to cited_smiles. Score differences are observed chemical associations under these conditions, not component attribution or an activation verdict.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted set is mostly medium-sized aromatic carboxamides: median 25 heavy atoms, range 1–40, with median three rings and three aromatic rings. There are 21 molecules below six heavy atoms and none above fifty. Seed 0 favors an indole-like fused tricycle bearing a pyridyl tertiary carboxamide; its best molecule has 24 heavy atoms and four rings. Seed 1 retains an indole carboxamide with a phenol, bromomethyl group and N-chloro N–N linkage. Seed 2 reaches vinyl/enyloxy-substituted indene-like carboxamides with a pyridyl terminus. These are recognizable amide/aromatic frameworks, but substitution patterns vary from fairly ordinary to chemically awkward. The Parent has the same median size and ring count. Child typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 194/101 versus Parent 187/70; N-halogen-bearing molecules decrease from 404 to 174, so this Child does not exhibit a general loss of ring variety or a uniform increase in that liability.
liabilities: The seed-1 best molecule contains an N–N–Cl unit and a benzylic bromide; other cited molecules include a peroxide/thioamide combination. Their presence warrants chemical scrutiny, not an assertion of measured instability.
The seed-0 high scorers add a fused unsaturated ring and tertiary amide substitutions; synthetic access and stereochemical/conformational consequences were not assessed.
missing_features: The weaker sampled molecules do not consistently preserve the compact aromatic amide/heteroaryl arrangement present in the better-scoring ones; this is uneven retention of an existing capability, not absence of rings or amides.

A broader set of chemically ordinary alternatives around the favorable heteroaryl amide topology is underdeveloped relative to N-halogen and bromomethyl variants. The data do not identify any unique required scaffold or prove that removing those substituents would raise the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145; the best fused N-hydroxymethyl pyridyl amide scores 0.5046949386828399. Its corresponding N-methyl analogue scores 0.458386638264238. However, on the methoxy fused scaffold the N-methyl compound scores 0.4811252243246881 and its N-hydroxymethyl version 0.4675469497082676, so a generic reward for adding hydroxymethyl is unsupported. The aromatic amide arrangement matters: the small difluoroacetanilide scores 1.1981624660071522e-08, and a much larger peroxide/thioamide-linked aromatic product scores 1.609251619261726e-11. Methane and difluorine score 0.0. Parent seed-best values are 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554, versus Child 0.5046949386828399, 0.44989726212142783 and 0.4330127018922193. The molecular evidence favors selected compact multi-ring amide arrangements over fragments or indiscriminate growth, with seed-dependent substitutions.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most heavily elaborated panel: median 46 heavy atoms, range 1–115, with median six rings and six aromatic rings. There are 271 molecules above fifty heavy atoms and 19 below six. The Parent median is 32 heavy atoms and four rings, with 18 above fifty and 23 below six. Child typed/generic scaffold counts are 410/313 versus Parent 347/241. Seed 1 high scorers are 53-heavy-atom heteroaromatic/lactam-like assemblies carrying several exocyclic alkenes, a terminal alkyne, an aldehyde, halogens and branched unsaturated substituents. Seed 0 also reaches a 53-heavy-atom best molecule, with linked carbonyl/ester-carbonate functionality, fused aromatic rings, an N–O linkage and N-fluorination. Seed 2 instead favors a 39-heavy-atom, seven-ring conjugated heterocycle with cyclic carbonyls, fluoromethyl, thioether and unsaturated side chains. These diverse graphs are much harder to regard as routine medicinal chemistry than the simpler amide/amine panels.
liabilities: The very large size tail, densely conjugated exocyclic alkenes, terminal alkynes, aldehydes and crowded substitution create substantial synthetic and conformational questions; no experimental route or stability data resolve them.

N-halogen-bearing accepted molecules number 246 versus Parent 39. The Parent itself contains unusual O–F, S–Br and nitroso motifs, so its higher endpoint is not evidence of better practical chemistry.
missing_features: The Child does not recover the Parent seed-0 combination of compact fused heterocyclic connectivity and much higher score. The gap is access to useful arrangements without extensive appendage growth, not absence of ring complexity.

Chemically ordinary, compact alternatives that retain the productive heteroatom/carbonyl topology are not established by this trajectory; exact-score ties across homologues show that some extra growth adds no observed benefit.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highest seed-1 molecule scores 0.6388726464740966; changing its terminal methoxy group to ethoxy leaves that score unchanged. Simple fragments such as methane and acetylene score 0.5, and the smaller vinyl bicyclic aza-aromatic scores 0.5048505159185113. Thus extensive heterocyclic decoration associates with higher scores in the Child stream, but some added substituent changes are score-neutral. Size itself is not a sufficient explanation: the Parent seed-0 best is a 30-heavy-atom fused nitrogen heterocycle scoring 0.8561477222467935, whereas Child seed 0 reaches 0.5966505582402932. Child seed-best values are 0.5966505582402932, 0.6388726464740966 and 0.6062699256110521, versus Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496. The observed score does not certify that the large conjugated structures are stable, synthesizable or drug-like.

per_task.generated_character: These molecules combine aromatic hydrophobic surfaces with unacylated aliphatic amines, often in saturated or partly unsaturated nitrogen rings. The set has median 32 heavy atoms, range 1–73, median four rings and two aromatic rings; 19 molecules are below six heavy atoms and 15 exceed fifty. The best seed-0 molecule is a 26-heavy-atom, three-ring chlorophenethyl-substituted aniline/thiophenol bearing an N-methylpyrrolidine and propyl group. Seeds 1 and 2 instead show azetidine-containing structures with aryl sulfoxides, halogenated aryl groups and larger carbocyclic units. The unacylated aliphatic-amine SMARTS flag occurs in 760 molecules versus Parent 722; this is a structural flag, not a pKa calculation. The Parent median size is 29, with the same median ring/aromatic-ring counts. Child typed/generic scaffolds are 353/212 versus Parent 327/202. Basic amine chemistry is abundant, and several high scorers look more conventionally medicinal than the oversized conjugated panel.
liabilities: Dense halogenation, aryl thiol/aniline substituents and sulfoxides coexist with crowded saturated rings. Their oxidation state, stereochemistry and practical synthesis require assessment beyond score.
Every digest charged and stereocentre flag is absent; this leaves protonation and stereochemical presentation unresolved, despite the abundant potentially basic amines.
missing_features: Low-scoring products lack the combination of an exposed aliphatic amine and the extended aromatic arrangement that the successful products already display; amine generation itself is not missing.

Stereochemically resolved alternatives for the substituted saturated rings and sulfoxides are not shown. Their value cannot be inferred from this neutral, stereounspecified trajectory, and no further target-specific pharmacophore is justified by these scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 N-methylpyrrolidine compound scores 0.9969811129341767, and its larger partly unsaturated nitrogen-ring analogue scores 0.9907712005460624. The seed-2 amine/azetidine sulfoxide scores 0.9906410741062175. In contrast, the N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine carboxamide scores 0.0002562175393167918, and the chlorinated aryl sulfonyl chloride scores 0.00039724860827780096. These comparisons associate high scores with exposed aliphatic amines plus connected aromatic surfaces, rather than halogenation or sulfonyl functionality alone. Child seed-best values are 0.9969811129341767, 0.9876203088351722 and 0.9906410741062175 versus Parent 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864. The trajectories do not establish a binding pose, measured receptor activity or a unique required ring.

per_task.generated_character: The panel contains medium-sized polycyclic heteroaromatic molecules linked to cyclic amide/diamide and amine-containing rings. Median size is 33 heavy atoms, range 1–69, with median five rings and two aromatic rings; ten molecules are below six heavy atoms and five exceed fifty. The seed-2 best is a 32-heavy-atom benzimidazole-like system linking a propyl/ethoxy phenyl ring to a saturated seven-membered cyclic diamide. Seed 0 instead has a fused pyrazole-containing aromatic/cyclic amide assembly, while seed 1 joins a quinoline-like system to a larger nitrogen/carbonyl-containing ring. The Parent median size is 31, with the same median ring counts. Child typed/generic scaffolds are 551/354 versus Parent 560/380. The scaffold distribution is not collapsed to one topology, although high-scoring examples repeatedly combine heteroaromatic and cyclic carbonyl motifs. Some examples have conventional functional groups; large or bridged ring closures make synthetic feasibility less certain.
liabilities: N-fluoro, N-chloro and N–S substitutions appear around otherwise recognizable cyclic diamide cores; these are chemical-quality concerns even where a score remains relatively high.

Highly bridged or expanded nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems have unspecified stereochemistry and untested synthetic accessibility. The low scores of tiny fragments also show that fragmentation does not supply the useful motif combination.
missing_features: Smaller or nonaromatic products fail to retain the aromatic heterocycle plus cyclic carbonyl arrangement seen in stronger molecules. More rings alone are not the missing ingredient.

The record does not establish a single absent functional group that would close the remaining score gap. The visible limitation is uneven exploration of heteroatom placement and ring connections using chemically credible substitutions.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best benzimidazole-like compound scores 0.25531389540169014; replacing one aromatic nitrogen with carbon gives 0.24856118317762688. An N-fluorinated cyclic-diamide variant also scores 0.24856118317762688, so that unusual bond is tolerated in a high-score neighborhood without demonstrating that it is beneficial. The seed-0 and seed-1 best values are 0.2183193397487884 and 0.2180368716314368. A smaller nonaromatic bridged amine/carbonyl/ether molecule scores 0.08878156117739505, and methane, ethylene and hydrogen peroxide score 0.0. The Parent seed-best values are 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313. The gradient suggests a useful combination of aromatic heteroatom placement and cyclic carbonyl-containing topology, with modest gains from local variants; the observed span does not disclose an unseen reference structure or uniquely missing feature.

per_task.generated_character: The set is dominated by nitrogen-rich fused heterocycles containing carbonyl and imino groups, fluorinated substituents, and partly unsaturated carbon rings. Median size is 27 heavy atoms, range 1–56, with median four rings and three aromatic rings. There are 21 molecules below six heavy atoms and one above fifty. The seed-2 best has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, with an N-fluorinated imino/lactam fused core and fluoromethyl-substituted cyclopentadiene-like ring. The seed-0 best has 27 heavy atoms and four rings, including an amidine-like group, pyridyl ring and N-fluorinated bicyclic carbonyl system. Seed 1 favors a 27-heavy-atom, five-ring fluorinated carbonyl heterocycle with an additional strained fused nitrogen ring. N-halogen-bearing molecules number 512 versus Parent 399, while the unacylated aliphatic-amine flag occurs in 124 versus Parent 254. The Parent median is 26 heavy atoms, four rings and two aromatic rings. Child typed/generic scaffolds are 262/128 versus Parent 275/102. This is abundant ring and nitrogen chemistry, but much of the nitrogen is imino, amide-like or halogenated rather than an ordinary aliphatic amine.
liabilities: Frequent N–F bonds, imines/amidine-like groups, dense unsaturation and occasional strained fused rings make these high scores weak evidence of practical medicinal quality. N-halogen frequency is an observed structural count, not a measured instability rate.

No explicit stereochemistry or charge state is shown; this is particularly limiting for substituted saturated rings and ionizable imino/amine functionality. An occasional very large merged product and tiny fluorine fragments occupy both size extremes.
missing_features: Ordinary aliphatic amine-bearing saturated ring alternatives are less represented than in the Parent, although they are demonstrably within the generator capability and accompany higher Parent endpoints on two seeds.

The Child does not demonstrate reliable access to compact, chemically conventional combinations of the useful fluorinated heterocycle and polar substituents without recurring N–F bonds and crowded unsaturation. No unique target structure or required stereoisomer can be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed-best values are 0.6062468812165027, 0.46571488311711784 and 0.613303371988598, versus Parent 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813. Both sides favor compact fluorinated nitrogen-rich systems over a 56-heavy-atom, nine-ring merged aromatic/lactam molecule scoring 3.7589249668299926e-42 or isolated fluorine scoring 1.1043196211273875e-26. The low organic seed-0 carbonyl-rich heterocycle scores 1.5661146385331196e-21 despite a size comparable to the better molecules. Thus appropriate co-occurrence of fluorination, heteroatom arrangement and molecular size matters more than merely adding nitrogen or rings. The higher Parent seed-0/1 best structures include fluorinated saturated or partly saturated amine rings alongside related fused imino/carbonyl cores; the Child favors more N-halogenated alternatives and shows fewer ordinary aliphatic amines. This is an association, not proof that an amine or a particular bond causes the endpoint difference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1f54bfad8351 versus code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, complete accepted Search seeds 0/1/2 at batch ten and 300 evaluations per session. The supplied high-score molecules include N-fluoro, N-chloro and N–N–Cl structures alongside conventional amide/amine examples. One accepted panel contains 512 N-halogen-bearing molecules versus Parent 399, while another decreases to 174 from 404. This is a condition-specific chemical-quality pattern, not a uniform Child change or an attributed component effect. Exact paths, hashes and motif definitions are in policy/scratch/r0054-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably pair productive ring and heteroatom arrangements with chemically ordinary substituent choices.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A future task-agnostic construction capability could preserve useful scaffold and heteroatom connections while offering conventional alternatives to reactive-looking heteroatom-halogen substitutions. Let current-session observations determine their value; neither a blanket ban nor a guaranteed score improvement follows from this chemistry association.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1f54bfad8351 and Parent n-cf8d309c06de, accepted Search seeds 0/1/2 under the same frozen profile. One panel grows to median 46 heavy atoms and 271 of 870 accepted optimizer molecules above fifty, versus Parent median 32 and 18 of 870. A smaller Parent best structure has a much higher observed score in the corresponding seed. Across panels, Child counts below six heavy atoms are 21, 19, 19, 10 and 21; this is a minority tail, not the dominant generated chemistry. Evidence and definitions remain in policy/scratch/r0054-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json; these observations do not establish an optimal size cutoff.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot consistently explore useful scaffold rearrangements without substantial molecular growth or loss into tiny fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general generator could expand access to size-preserving ring edits, connected substitutions and controlled simplification while retaining the scored functional-group arrangement. Measure both fragment and oversized tails using all accepted products; do not substitute a fixed size preference or a task-specific template for session feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1f54bfad8351 versus Parent n-cf8d309c06de, complete accepted Search seeds 0/1/2, same budget and batch size. One Child panel carries the unacylated aliphatic-amine structural flag in 760 of 870 molecules, compared with Parent 722, so a global inability to generate amines would be false. Another panel contains 124 versus Parent 254 and shifts toward N-halogen/imino chemistry, while higher Parent seed-best molecules include amine-bearing rings. The SMARTS definition and exact input provenance are in policy/scratch/r0054-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json; this is neither a pKa measurement nor proof of causal score benefit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ordinary aliphatic amine-ring chemistry is available but is not retained evenly across the high-scoring families the generator explores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could maintain access to saturated amine rings and preserve their attachment topology during scaffold changes, alongside amide and heteroaromatic alternatives. Which forms are retained must depend on paid observations in the current session, without universal amine enrichment or objective-identity rules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1f54bfad8351, supplied digest covering accepted Search seeds 0/1/2 under the frozen batch-ten profile. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0, despite substituted saturated rings, sulfoxides, amines and imino groups in the cited molecules. This establishes an output-representation gap only; neutral notation does not prove nonionizability, and the scores do not show that explicit states would improve an objective.
transferable_gaps.gap: The reported molecular outputs do not resolve stereochemical identity or explicitly represented ionization states.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: If stereochemical or ionization-state generation is developed later, it should be chemically valid, de novo and subject to the same canonical uniqueness and session-isolation rules. Its value requires measured evidence; an assumed preferred stereoisomer or protonation state is not supplied by this report.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
